newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares slip in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares slip in sluggish trade.

text.p: 1800 GMT - Portuguese shares slipped lower in uneventful trade but dealers said the market might be pausing for breath before heading higher.
*"The market seems to be indifferent to all the good news that ought to be pushing it up," said one dealer.

*"There was some profit-taking going on today but we should head higher soon," said another trader. "Conditions for investing in shares remain good: interest rates are falling, the market outlook is positive elsewhere and the economy is in good shape for the single currency in 1999."
*Bank of Portugal governor Antonio de Sousa said it was perfectly "acheivable" for Portugal to be among the first group of countries to adopt the European Union's single currency.
*PSI20 index .PSI20 index finished down 0.25 percent at 4,943.98 points.
*Portucel slipped 5 escudos to 935 on turnover of 160,814.

*BTA ended down 3 esc at 2,702 with 123,066 shares traded. The bank saw the final phase of its privatisation completed today with the sale of a 13.22 percent stake at a fixed price of 2,630 escudos per share.
*Shares in Sonae Investimentos hit a year high of 4,744 escudos but retreated to end at 4,719, up 29 esc on their previous close, in volume of 89,770.
*Analysts said shares in the industrial group could reach an all-time high of 5,000 escudos by the end of this year as investors anticipate the advantages of a reorganisation of the group.
*PSI20 December futures were down one point at 4,989.
